name: VA-08
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's D+26 partisan lean in Northern Virginia
Incumbent Don Beyer running again with no serious opposition
Prediction markets price Democratic win near 96%
model.rationale: This is one of the most Democratic-leaning House districts in Virginia, and incumbent Don Beyer has a roughly 100-to-1 fundraising advantage over Republican Tony Sabio, who has almost no cash on hand. Markets price a Beyer win at about 96%, and the absence of any competitive polling or expert attention signals a race with little suspense.
model.watch: Only a dramatic national wave or unforeseen development involving the incumbent could meaningfully narrow the margin, and even that is unlikely to threaten the outcome.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Northern Virginia's 8th District is a deeply Democratic seat, with a partisan lean of D+26, and Don Beyer has held it comfortably since 2015. He enters the general election renominated, with about $839,000 in cash after raising more than $2.1 million. Republican Tony Sabio has raised roughly $22,000, leaving him with minimal resources for a competitive campaign. An independent candidate and a Libertarian are also on the ballot, but neither shows meaningful fundraising or infrastructure.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings exist for this race, which itself reflects how little contestation is expected. Prediction markets put Beyer's chances near 96%. With the incumbent's financial dominance, the district's strong partisan tilt, and token opposition, the seat is rated safely Democratic.
